can you make this into a clear prompt for writing a delivery handoff note for the morning driver and the crew at our market stall. i don't need you to write the actual note now, just clean up the request so someone can do it. the finished note should be practical enough to use on the delivery run, not a general description of the market or a message to customers. it should be brief, but include the details below that change what the driver is supposed to do. the note itself should be the only thing returned when this prompt is used, with no intro or explanation around it.

this is for stall 14 at the east arcade of Bellweather Covered Market. the stall sells fruit, and this delivery is coming from Alder Vale Orchard on Thursday morning, 12 June. Mara Bell is the stall keeper and the person the driver should contact if the delivery cannot go straight to the stall. The driver is Leon Price. The market opens to shoppers at 6:00, but that isn't the decision time for the delivery. The useful check is the north service gate at 5:30 a.m. Please don't turn the opening time into a condition or make the route depend on whether shoppers have arrived.

the load is 18 stackable green crates of pears, described on the orchard slip as early-season green pears. all 18 crates are intended for stall 14, not a split delivery to another stall. the crates are already labeled with the stall number, so the note doesn't need to ask the driver to relabel them or add a second label. mention the load clearly enough that nobody mistakes it for the apples due at another arcade later in the morning. there are no apples in this particular load, and don't make up a price, grade, or weight for the pears.

the delivery window is 5:20 to 5:45 a.m. on that Thursday. the driver should check the north service gate at exactly 5:30 a.m. for the route decision, even if the truck arrives a few minutes earlier or later within the window. i want the timing and condition stated plainly so the crew doesn't read the window itself as permission to unload anywhere. please don't say the delivery is already accepted or that the gate will definitely be open; we don't know that yet.

if the north service gate is fully open at 5:30, the requested action is to take all 18 crates through that gate and deliver them to stall 14. unloading at the stall is permitted only on that condition. the driver can then set the crates against the blue rail on the east side of the stall. keep the access aisle clear, with at least 1.2 metres of clear width, and don't put any crates in front of the neighboring flower stall's shutter. i think the blue rail is a helpful placement reference, so retain it rather than replacing it with a vague instruction to leave the crates nearby.

there are some handling points for the open-gate route too. leave the crates stacked no more than three high, with the labels facing outward so the stall crew can count them without moving the whole stack. don't open the crates, wash the pears, sort them, or transfer fruit between crates. the crew will do any checking after the handoff. the driver should not put the load inside the stall tent, because the back counter is being used for the scale and there isn't room there before opening. don't add extra equipment or ask the driver to carry the crates beyond the rail.

if the north service gate is shut, or only partly open, at 5:30, don't take the crates to stall 14, don't leave them by the gate, and don't wait for someone to open it. use a different action instead: take all 18 crates to Riverside Produce Depot, receiving bay C, and call Mara Bell at 07700 900 418 to tell her they have been taken there. that's the fallback, not a second choice to mention as equally available when the gate is fully open. the condition includes a gate that is only partly open; it isn't enough for the driver to be able to squeeze through. don't add another fallback location or suggest returning the load to the orchard.

for either route, the person making the note can tell the driver to record the crate count and whether any crates are visibly damaged. don't ask the driver to estimate the number of damaged pears inside the crates, since they're meant to stay shut. the note can say that any visible crate damage should be reported to Mara, but don't imply there is damage now. no need to include pricing, an invoice process, or a signature requirement. those aren't part of the decision or the physical handoff, and no invoice information has been supplied.

Mara Bell is the stall keeper. there are a couple of interaction details to keep in view. someone may open the preference and see Nadia highlighted from an earlier session, so the writer should make the intended change to Orson easy to understand without suggesting Nadia is a bad or forbidden account generally. the exclusion applies to this user’s stated preference only: the digest should go to Orson, not Nadia. the group address remains an option in the list, but it isn’t the requested recipient either. don’t make Nadia disappear from the choices and don’t call the group address a backup. if there is no selection, ask the user to choose; don’t silently fill in a recipient.

hey, can you help me turn this into a clear task for the inventory workbook at Cedar Street Food Cooperative? we need a draft proposed restock list for the regular shelf-stable pantry goods, not a purchase order and not a general report about the whole co-op. the list is for the volunteers who set up the next Saturday pickup, so it should help them see which ordinary pantry items may need replenishing. please keep the task limited to the 18 pantry SKUs on the “Shelf stock” tab. the produce tables, refrigerated items, household supplies, and the separate community reserve shelf are outside this request. Mara said, “please don’t treat the reserve shelf as regular stock.” that matters because volunteers sometimes count the reserve jars when they’re moving boxes, but those jars are not part of the regular shelf inventory.

the workbook is called `May_Week3_Count.xlsx`. it has the tabs “Shelf stock,” “Min levels,” and “Receiving,” and the latest count is meant to be the Saturday, May 18 count at 3 p.m. use that workbook and those tabs, not last week’s paper tally that’s still clipped by the stockroom door. the “Shelf stock” tab has the 18 item names and recorded quantities; “Min levels” has the floor level for each item and the case pack size; “Receiving” is where deliveries through Friday, May 17 should have been entered. i don’t want you to assume those tabs are all complete just because they’re in the workbook. the condition for making the restock list is a little specific, and if it isn’t met we need a different useful thing instead.

first, all 18 listed pantry items need to have a physical count recorded for the May 18 count. second, the count needs to have both required initials: Mara, the shift lead, and Inez, the stockroom volunteer. it’s not enough if one person initialed or if their initials are just on the top of an old page. third, deliveries received through Friday the 17th need to be entered on the “Receiving” tab so the count is not missing stock that has already arrived. please check that the item entries and the receiving records line up; a blank count, a missing initial, or an obvious unresolved difference between the tabs means the condition has not been met. all three checks have to hold before you make any proposed order quantities. don’t treat a partial match as approval to go ahead.

if and only if all those checks hold, make the proposed restock list for the 18 pantry SKUs. compare each recorded on-hand quantity with that item’s minimum level, and include the items that are below their floor, with the gap and a suggested order quantity. use the case pack size shown for that item in the workbook and round a needed quantity up to a whole case; show the unit clearly so a volunteer doesn’t mistake cases for individual cans or bags. use the vendor shown in the workbook if it has one, but leave that field blank if there is no vendor entered. don’t add items just because you think they’re popular, and don’t suggest more than the amount needed to bring an item up to its minimum level after rounding to the case pack. this is only a proposed list for review, not an instruction to place an order or promise that stock will be available.

if any part of the condition fails, don’t make a restock list, don’t calculate proposed order quantities, and don’t use guesses to fill the gap. instead make a verification checklist for the affected item or records. say which SKU or receiving entry needs attention and what is missing or doesn’t line up, such as a physical count, one of the two initials, or a Friday delivery entry. if you can’t identify a particular SKU because a tab or record is missing, name the missing tab or record rather than inventing an item. that checklist is the useful next step for the stockroom team to complete before the count is ready; it isn’t a second version of the proposed order list.

some practical details: the normal pickup crew sorts shelf-stable groceries on Friday evening, then checks the list before the Saturday setup. there are 18 regular pantry lines, including dry staples and canned goods, but please rely on the workbook for their actual item names and values rather than writing a made-up example list. some stock may be on a cart while a delivery is being put away, which is why the receiving check matters. don’t count a delivery twice if it is already reflected in the Saturday quantity. the reserve shelf is separately managed, and this task doesn’t move reserve goods into regular stock or ask for a reserve transfer. also, if the workbook’s case sizes differ between products, apply each product’s own case size rather than one general pack assumption.

for the result, give us just one artifact: either the proposed restock list when every condition is satisfied, or the verification checklist when at least one condition is not satisfied. make the chosen artifact easy to scan by item, and include a short status line saying which path applies and, for the checklist path, which check failed. the restock list should show the SKU or item name, current quantity, minimum level, gap, suggested case quantity, unit, and vendor when listed; the checklist should show the affected item or record and the specific thing to verify. don’t add a narrative summary, a separate recommendation, or a purchasing note after the artifact. if a required workbook value is blank, keep it blank or identify it in the checklist as appropriate rather than supplying a value from memory.

the team needs to review this before Monday at 10 a.m., when the stockroom volunteers plan the week’s receiving space. that timing is the reason for asking for a usable draft now, but it does not change the checks above or make an incomplete count good enough for order quantities. keep zero quantities as zero, don’t convert units unless the workbook gives a pack size, and don’t include the older paper tally as a second source of current stock. the task is just to produce the one conditional inventory artifact from the specified workbook; it should leave the volunteers with either a reviewable draft list or clear verification work, depending on whether the stated condition holds.","response":"Create one inventory artifact for Cedar Street Food Cooperative using `May_Week3_Count.xlsx`. The artifact must be either a proposed restock list or, if the condition below is not satisfied, a verification checklist. Do not create a purchase order or a general inventory report.

## Scope and source

Use only the 18 regular shelf-stable pantry SKUs on the “Shelf stock” tab. Exclude produce, refrigerated items, household supplies, and the separately managed community reserve shelf. As Mara said, “please don’t treat the reserve shelf as regular stock.” Do not count reserve goods as regular inventory or suggest transferring them.

Check that the item entries and receiving records line up. Do not assume that a tab is complete simply because it is present.

## Required condition

Make a proposed restock list only if all of the following checks hold:

1. Each of the 18 pantry items has a physical count recorded for the May 18 count.
2. Both Mara, the shift lead, and Inez, the stockroom volunteer, have provided the required initials for the count. One initial, or initials only on an old page, is not sufficient.
3. Deliveries received through Friday, May 17, are entered on the “Receiving” tab, and the item entries and receiving records line up without an obvious unresolved difference.

A blank count, a missing initial, or an unresolved difference between the tabs means the condition has not been met. All three checks are required; do not proceed with proposed quantities on the basis of a partial match.

Leave the vendor field blank if none is entered. Do not add items based on popularity or suggest more than is needed to reach the minimum after rounding to the case pack. This is a proposed list for review, not an instruction to order or a promise of availability.

## If the condition is not satisfied

Do not make a restock list or calculate proposed order quantities. Instead, prepare a verification checklist for the affected items or records. Identify the SKU or receiving entry that needs attention and specify what is missing or does not line up, such as a physical count, one of the required initials, or a Friday delivery entry. If a tab or record is missing and a particular SKU cannot be identified, name the missing tab or record rather than inventing an item. This checklist is the next step for the stockroom team; it is not a second version of the proposed order list.

## Output and handling

Provide just one artifact: the proposed restock list if every required check holds, or the verification checklist if any check fails. Make it easy to scan by item. Include a short status line identifying which path applies and, for a checklist, which check failed. Do not add a narrative summary, separate recommendation, or purchasing note after the artifact.

Use the workbook’s actual item names and values rather than made-up examples. If a required value is blank, leave it blank or identify it in the checklist as appropriate; do not supply a value from memory. Keep zero quantities as zero. Do not count a delivery twice if it is already reflected in the Saturday quantity, and use each product’s own case size where pack sizes differ. Stock may be on a cart while a delivery is being put away, so account for the receiving check without assuming the delivery is missing or already counted.

The team needs to review the artifact before Monday at 10 a.m., when stockroom volunteers plan the week’s receiving space. This timing does not change the required checks or make an incomplete count sufficient for proposed order quantities. The task is limited to producing the one conditional inventory artifact from the specified workbook, leaving the volunteers with either a reviewable draft list or clear verification work." ,"reasoning":null}
